ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the EU consolidated sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated lists, Spanish FIU (SEPBLAC) risk indicators, and FATF guidance; PEP status assessed per Article 4 of Ley 10/2010 applying a 5-year in-office plus post-employment standard; OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions screened as an international banking compliance overlay; enhanced due diligence files retained for 10 years per Article 25 of Ley 10/2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC), Madrid - www.rmc.es (online application for Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social; also available through any Spanish notary or the registered intermediary)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate denomination must be expressed in Spanish or in any language using Latin-alphabet characters; non-Latin scripts (Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic, etc.) must be phonetically transliterated into Spanish characters; the name must be grammatically compatible with the legal-form indicator 'Sociedad Limitada' / 'SL' and must not reproduce, wholly or partially, any existing registered corporate name or distinctive sign in the RMC index.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Seguro(s), Aseguradora, Reaseguradora (requires prior approval of the insurance supervisory authority)
Banco, Caja (reserved for licensed credit institutions)
Sociedad Anónima / SA and Sociedad Limitada / SL (legal-form tokens cannot be embedded in the corporate name)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RMC negative certificate reserves the denomination for 60 days from issuance; the applicant may re-apply for a renewed certificate while the RMC internal hold remains, with the total reservation period not exceeding 6 months. If the application is rejected on grounds of identity or similarity with an existing registered name, or because of a prohibited/sensitive token, the applicant may (i) file a new modified denomination request through the RMC online portal, or (ii) lodge a hierarchical administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) within one month of rejection notice, attaching the refusal decision, the proposed denomination, and proof of legitimate interest. After exhaustion of administrative remedies, judicial review may be sought before the Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not accepted as the sole corporate seat for an operating entity. The SL must fix a domicilio social in Spain where its effective administration is located or its principal establishment sits. Administrative virtual offices are tolerable only alongside a declared, physically operative warehouse for the kitting/assembly activity; AEAT will attribute Spanish tax residence based on actual material and management substance, so a purely virtual seat is untenable for this 3PL business model.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: Low-to-Moderate - estimated 15-20% probability of unannounced AEAT or municipal inspectors visiting the operating warehouse within the first 24 months of activity; SEPBLAC on-site AML inspection probability for a Low_Risk_Standard warehousing/kitting entity is below 10%; municipal licensing and fire-safety control visits at warehouse commencement are estimated at approximately 25%.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Compliance with basic workplace safety regulations; no specific fire safety certification required for low-risk assembly

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), official portal https://www.aeat.es/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident entities obtain CIF/NIF by appointing a Spanish tax representative and submitting registration application to AEAT with corporate documents, power of attorney, and proof of legal existence. Online portal available for eligible applicants.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box; tax classification follows legal form under Spanish law. Hybrid mismatch provisions under Council Directive (EU) 2017/952 apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 50,000 EUR annual turnover threshold for mandatory registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory facturación electrónica for all VAT-registered entities. Real-time electronic reporting to AEAT through certified platforms or APIs, including digital invoice stamping and clearance procedures.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate for goods exported outside the EU, proven by dispatch proof and customs export declaration. Offshore services may qualify if performed abroad and invoiced accordingly.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ED), Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document, Proof of inward remittance or payment receipt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Administrative penalties of 100% of evaded tax plus interest. Retrospective revocation of zero-rating status and clawback of undue VAT credits if export documentation is incomplete or fraudulent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) and the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCOM, Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business). The Banco de España is the national foreign-exchange and monetary authority; DGCOM manages foreign-investment registration and statistical compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. Spain applies EU capital-movement freedoms under Articles 63–66 TFEU; no prior administrative authorization is required for inbound or outbound capital, except a mandatory ex-post statistical declaration to the Banco de España/DGCOM for foreign direct investments (form DP-2) and for foreign investment in Spanish resident companies exceeding EUR 3,000,000 (or where shareholders are from non-transparent or flag-of-convenience jurisdictions). Profit remittances are unrestricted, subject to the 19% Spanish corporate withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders (reduced under applicable tax treaties), and must be documented with a certificate of tax residence and proof of tax compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion requirements apply in Spain. Exporters may receive and retain foreign-currency proceeds in bank accounts opened at resident credit institutions; however, any export settlement exceeding EUR 12,500 per operation or an aggregate of EUR 1,000,000 per month must be reported on the monthly Banco de España balance-of-payments declaration. There are no forced conversion ratios or repatriation deadlines, although for anti-money-laundering and corporate-tax purposes all export receipts must be fully booked and traceable to the underlying commercial contract.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility as an ancillary payment rail only. EU-licensed e-money institutions (e.g., Airwallex, Wise) may passport into Spain under PSD2 and can provide multi-currency payment accounts, accelerated cross-border receipts, and FX conversion. Legal constraints: (i) EMIs are not credit institutions and cannot extend credit or offer interest-bearing accounts; (ii) the SL’s principal treasury account and tax/legal-domicile link must remain with a Spanish or EU-passported credit institution; (iii) Spanish AML Law 10/2010 may require a binding link between the EMI wallet and the bank account for high-value transactions. For a standard 3PL kitting entity, the EMI is an approved settlement sub-channel but cannot serve as the sole banking partner.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance is generally mandatory for at least one most senior signatory director (or the appointed attorney with sufficient powers) at the initial bank interview in Spain. Under Law 10/2010 and EBA Regulatory Technical Standards, identification may be completed remotely by videoconference if both parties use qualified electronic signature certificates and the process is independently recorded; however, most Tier-1 Spanish banks require a face-to-face meeting for companies with non-European shareholders. Non-resident directors must first obtain an NIE and must either appear in person at the bank or execute a notarized general power of attorney (poder) in favor of an on-site representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: shareholding layer involving non-EEA corporate shareholders or nominees.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified, legalized corporate charter and registry excerpt (certificado de registro mercantil) of each corporate shareholder; complete shareholders' register with individual TIE/NIE numbers; signed beneficial-ownership attestation letter; organizational chart showing the full UBO chain to a natural person; notarized and apostilled proof of beneficial ownership, with simplified clearance for lean and transparent holding structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Activity mismatch: declared ISIC 5210 (warehousing and kitting) versus high-value cross-border transaction patterns inconsistent with ordinary logistics operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial agreements with customers and suppliers; warehouse lease or sub-lease contract; insured inventory report; sample purchase orders and bills of lading; corporate VAT/CENSAL declaration; last fiscal year corporate tax return; and a board-approved business plan validating the outsourced fulfillment, kitting, and assembly operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds uncertainty for inbound capital contributions from overseas groups.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial deed of capital increase (escritura) with bank deposit certificate; audited or management financial statements of the contributing shareholder; source-of-funds report issued by the paying bank or EMD; tax-residence certificate of the investor; adverse-media and sanctions screening results for all board members and beneficial owners; completed EG-3 or DP-2 declaration to the DGCOM when applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant route for an equity contribution from a foreign parent: (i) execute a notarial deed of capital increase and deposit the capital with the Spanish Banco de España account or a resident notary's escrow to subscribe the new shares; (ii) remit funds via SWIFT MT103 from the investing company’s bank to the SL’s account, using purpose code 'EQUI' or the Banco de España balance-of-payments classification for equity injection; (iii) include the corporate NIF (CIF), deed reference, and the SL’s IBAN in the narrative field; (iv) for investments exceeding EUR 3,000,000, file the post-investment declaration with the DGCOM (form DP-2) and ensure shareholders are not from tax-haven or high-risk jurisdictions; (v) record the funds as paid-in share capital as of the notarial date, with no early repayment or refund for at least two years unless followed by a valid capital-reduction proceeding.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For routine supplier and trade settlements: SEPA Credit Transfer for EEA counterparties and SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA payments. For high-value or documentary transactions (e.g., raw-material purchase or export financing), an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (payable at sight, issued through a Spanish advising bank) is appropriate. All outbound payments must be reported on the monthly Banco de España balance-of-payments declaration when the amount exceeds EUR 12,500; tax authorities require proof that each payment corresponds to an invoice, logistics contract, or bona fide commercial liability. Payments to affiliated parties must comply with Spanish transfer-pricing rules (Article 41 of the Corporate Income Tax Law) and be supported by benchmarking studies where applicable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot EUR/FX conversion lines (T+2) for settlement of export proceeds and supplier payments
Outright foreign-exchange forwards (vanilla, up to 18 months, with a documented underlying commercial exposure)
Cross-currency swaps (principal and interest-exchange, limited to foreign-currency debt and treasury obligations)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies subject to formal transfer or convertibility restrictions, settled in EUR
European-style FX options (purchased, not written, to hedge actual or expected payment flows, on a fully collateralized basis)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months and 25 days after the end of the tax year; calendar-year entities must file by 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers graduated surcharges of 5% per month up to 50% of the assessed tax, plus default interest; may lead to tax enforcement and administrative penalties, but does not by itself cause strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve annual accounts within 6 months after year-end; filing to the Mercantile Registry must occur within 1 month after approval; for calendar-year SLs, practical filing deadline is 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing leads to closure of the company's registry record (hoja registral cerrada), blocking subsequent filings; persistent failure for two consecutive years may trigger administrative dissolution and director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Declaración de Titularidad Real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Central through the Provincial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually together with the annual accounts; deadline coincides with the annual accounts filing deadline (31 July for calendar-year SLs).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or false statements are subject to anti-money laundering fines under Ley 10/2010; inaccurate beneficial ownership data may invalidate corporate filings and attract supervisory sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Applicable when transactions with any third party exceed EUR 3,005.06; filing window is between 1 February and 1 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate filings attract penalties ranging from EUR 100 up to EUR 20,000 depending on materiality and intent.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit for two consecutive years when an SL meets at least two of the following thresholds: total assets exceed EUR 2,850,000; net turnover exceeds EUR 5,700,000; average number of employees exceeds 50. Public-interest and regulated entities are subject to audit regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General Contable) approved by Real Decreto 1514/2007, consistent with EU-IFRS; consolidated accounts of groups use IFRS-EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must confirm beneficial ownership annually as part of the annual accounts filing to the Mercantile Registry. Any intermediate shareholding transfer or change in ultimate beneficial owner must be recorded in the internal UBO register and filed with the Mercantile Registry using the official RTR form.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax rate for Spanish resident companies, including a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly incorporated entities generally qualify for a 15% rate during the first profitable tax period and the immediately following tax period, subject to statutory eligibility conditions. Qualifying start-ups under the Start-ups Law may generally apply a 15% rate for the first four profitable tax periods, subject to certification and eligibility requirements. Additional incentives may include research and development credits, technological innovation credits, employment incentives, capitalization reserve deductions, and double-taxation relief. The reduced rate does not generally apply to entities classified as patrimonial entities or to entities continuing a previously conducted activity through restructuring designed to obtain the incentive.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite. Spanish tax losses may generally be carried forward without a fixed expiry period, subject to ownership-change limitations, anti-abuse rules, utilization caps, and minimum taxable-income requirements. Ordinary utilization is generally capped at 70% of positive taxable income, with a EUR 1 million minimum offset amount; additional limits apply to companies with higher net turnover.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Spanish Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) electronic headquarters using an electronic certificate, Cl@ve where available, or an authorized tax representative.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year company ending on 31 December, the ordinary filing period is 1 to 25 July of the following year. If the 25th is not a business day, the electronic deadline is generally extended to the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate tax identification number, legal name, registered office, tax period start and end dates, activity classification, filing type, and applicable regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Spanish SL is resident and must identify itself by its Spanish NIF. Foreign shareholders are reported through ownership and related-party disclosures and do not convert the SL into a non-resident taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before tax derived from statutory accounts prepared under the Spanish General Accounting Plan or applicable approved accounting framework.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish resident company's standalone accounting result. Do not substitute the foreign parent's consolidated result.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and deductions for non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, impairment, exempt income, tax credits, related-party corrections, and other book-to-tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Spanish tax rules to the SL's local accounts. Cross-border charges must be supported by contracts, benefit evidence, arm's-length pricing, and withholding-tax analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses from prior periods applied against current positive taxable income, subject to statutory utilization caps and ownership-change restrictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document the originating periods, amounts, prior utilization, ownership history, and any restructuring that could restrict utilization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result after permanent and temporary adjustments, applicable exemptions, deductions, and tax-loss utilization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign-parent income unless legally attributable to the Spanish SL. Include income from Spanish operations, inventory, fulfillment, kitting, packaging, service fees, and other activities conducted by the SL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax rate and gross tax liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable statutory or preferential rate multiplied by the taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% unless a valid preferential regime applies. The 15% newly created-entity rate must be separately substantiated and must not be applied automatically.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic or treaty-based relief for qualifying foreign taxes, withholding taxes, research and development, technological innovation, employment, and other statutory credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain foreign tax certificates and payment evidence. Credit claims are limited by Spanish statutory caps and the relevant treaty or domestic rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish tax withheld from income received and advance corporate tax payments, principally Modelo 202 or, for consolidated groups, Modelo 222.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all Spanish withholding certificates and installment payments to the annual return. Foreign shareholder-level withholding is not normally entered as an SL credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Required disclosure of related-party transactions, transaction categories, amounts, counterparties, and valuation information, including information forms where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report transactions with foreign shareholders, group companies, directors, and entities under common control. Reconcile disclosures to transfer-pricing records, invoices, and general ledger accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final amount payable, refundable, or available for statutory credit or future use, together with bank account and payment instructions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use a Spanish or SEPA-compatible account for payment or refund where required. A refund claim should be supported by reconciliations and evidence of withholding or advance payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic submission of the return and required financial-accounting information, including balance sheet, profit and loss account, and relevant schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure consistency with accounts filed with the Commercial Registry, VAT records, payroll records, and customs or logistics documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior AEAT assessment generally attracts a fixed surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay, with a 15% maximum after more than 12 months; after 12 months, late-payment interest is generally added. If an assessment is issued, penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, subject to aggravating or mitigating factors. Failure to file, inaccurate filing, or failure to pay can also trigger collection surcharges, interest, audit assessments, and criminal exposure where tax fraud thresholds are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, corporate income tax installment-payment form, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally 1 to 20 April, October, and December. If payment is made by bank direct debit, the practical deadline is generally earlier under AEAT payment-calendar rules. The installment is calculated under the prior-year tax-liability method or the current-period taxable-income method when mandatory or elected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, legal name, tax period, financial year, and applicable corporate tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL files in its own name; foreign ownership is not a substitute for the SL's NIF.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax liability or current-period accounting and tax result, depending on the applicable calculation method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the method required by Spanish law and confirm whether the entity exceeded statutory turnover thresholds or made a valid election.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Percentage of the statutory base after deducting eligible credits and prior installment payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain calculation schedules and reconcile the aggregate installments to Modelo 200.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount payable, bank account, payment reference, and electronic submission confirmation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use an authorized payment method and retain the NRC or equivalent electronic payment evidence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment may generate collection surcharges and late-payment interest. Failure to submit an accurate installment declaration can produce an assessment and tax penalties, with the final liability reconciled in Modelo 200.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Spanish resident company to a non-resident recipient, subject to domestic exemptions and treaty relief. Dividends paid to a qualifying EU or European Economic Area parent may qualify for the Spanish implementation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, generally requiring at least a 5% participation held for the statutory minimum period and satisfaction of anti-abuse, subject-to-tax, and beneficial-ownership conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership and treaty eligibility, confirm participation and holding-period conditions, and retain corporate ownership, substance, and anti-abuse evidence. Apply the reduced treaty rate at source only where Spanish administrative requirements are satisfied; otherwise withhold 19% and permit the recipient to seek a refund through the applicable AEAT procedure. Treaty relief does not apply merely because the recipient is incorporated in a treaty jurisdiction. The Spanish payer remains responsible for correct withholding, reporting, and payment through the relevant withholding forms, principally Modelo 216 and annual information reporting through Modelo 296.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic non-resident income tax withholding rate is generally 24% on Spanish-source royalties and similar intellectual-property income, and 19% on interest and other capital income, subject to statutory exemptions. Interest and royalty payments between associated companies resident in qualifying EU Member States may be exempt under the Spanish implementation of the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, normally requiring qualifying legal forms, a minimum 25% direct or indirect participation or common-parent relationship, a statutory holding period, subject-to-tax status, beneficial ownership, and anti-abuse compliance. Applicable tax treaties commonly reduce rates, often to 0% to 10% for interest and 0% to 10% for royalties, but the exact rate depends on the recipient's jurisdiction, beneficial ownership, treaty article, and income classification. Payments must also satisfy Spanish transfer-pricing, deductibility, documentation, and anti-hybrid rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Spain generally requires related-party transaction documentation unless an applicable statutory exemption applies. A principal quantitative exemption applies where the aggregate value of transactions with the same related person does not exceed EUR 250,000 at arm's length value during the tax period, subject to important exclusions and anti-abuse limitations. Spanish local-file obligations are generally relaxed or simplified for companies with net turnover below EUR 45 million, but documentation may still be required for material, exceptional, or specifically excluded transactions. A master file is generally relevant for Spanish entities belonging to groups with net turnover of at least EUR 45 million. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of at least EUR 750 million. The threshold does not eliminate the arm's-length requirement.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other methods and valuation techniques may be accepted where the selected method is the most appropriate method and is supported by reliable comparability analysis.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a single standalone Economic Substance Regulation regime equivalent to certain offshore regimes. Substance is nevertheless relevant under the Spanish General Tax Law anti-abuse provisions, beneficial-ownership standards, treaty anti-abuse rules, the EU Parent-Subsidiary and Interest-Royalties regimes, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation rules, and the principal-purpose test where applicable. A Spanish SL conducting fulfillment, kitting, packaging, inventory management, or 3PL services should maintain genuine personnel, premises, equipment, operational decision-making, accounting records, commercial risk, and evidence of functions performed. Conduit arrangements, circular financing, artificial royalty chains, non-arm's-length management charges, and entities lacking operational capacity present elevated challenge risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of revenue, false invoices, fictitious expenses, undeclared related-party income, manipulation of inventory, or deliberate underpayment of corporate tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of unpaid tax, with interest and collection measures. Tax fraud becomes criminal where the defrauded tax exceeds EUR 120,000 for a tax period; ordinary aggravated tax fraud may carry imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded. Particularly aggravated cases, including amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 or organized structures, may carry imprisonment of two to six years and a fine of two to six times the amount defrauded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability, civil restitution, fines, disqualification from public office or management, and subsidiary tax liability under Spanish tax law. Asset seizure and judicial precautionary measures may apply. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be ordered by a court in appropriate criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False invoicing, accounting fraud, or documentary falsification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or accepting invoices for services not provided, altering warehouse records, fabricating customs or logistics documents, or maintaining parallel accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax penalties, denial of deductions or input VAT, reassessment, interest, and potential criminal prosecution for accounting or document falsification. Criminal sanctions may include imprisonment and fines depending on the offense, amount, intent, and participation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, finance officers, and other participants may face personal criminal liability, civil compensation, fines, professional disqualification, and subsidiary tax liability. Corporate limitation of liability does not protect intentional personal misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially shifting fulfillment margins to a foreign affiliate through unsupported management fees, royalties, financing charges, inventory transfers, or underpriced or overpriced logistics services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may adjust taxable income to arm's length, deny deductions, impose interest, and impose specific transfer-pricing documentation or valuation penalties. Penalties can be calculated by reference to the undisclosed or incorrectly valued transaction and may be capped or increased according to the nature of the documentation breach.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable where they knowingly approve abusive arrangements, conceal records, or cause tax damage. Ordinary pricing disagreement does not automatically create personal liability, but deliberate manipulation may support civil, administrative, or criminal claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, management fees, or other Spanish-source income to non-residents without withholding, without validating treaty residence, or without filing withholding returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish payer may owe the unwithheld tax, late-payment interest, filing penalties, and, depending on the circumstances, penalties generally calculated as a percentage of the amount not withheld or not paid. Treaty relief can be denied where residence, beneficial ownership, or anti-abuse conditions are not proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives may incur subsidiary liability where the failure resulted from their culpable conduct or where statutory liability conditions are met. Personal liability is not automatic merely because the company failed to withhold.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying kitting or packaging services, claiming fictitious input VAT, suppressing stock movements, misdeclaring import values, or incorrectly applying intra-Community or export treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, denial of credits, penalties, interest, customs debt, import duties, seizure, and potential criminal tax fraud where thresholds and intent requirements are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and customs representatives may face personal or subsidiary liability for intentional or negligent misconduct, including civil recovery, administrative fines, and criminal prosecution in serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, treaty abuse, or lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Spanish SL as a conduit with no meaningful personnel, premises, decision-making, operating assets, or commercial risk while routing dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees to another jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or EU-directive benefits, withholding-tax reassessment, corporate tax adjustments, interest, anti-abuse penalties, and possible application of Spanish general anti-avoidance or conflict-in-application rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil and tax liability for deliberate abuse, fraudulent documentation, or asset stripping. Criminal liability requires satisfaction of the relevant statutory offense and intent thresholds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify the ultimate beneficial owner, accepting unexplained funds, using opaque payment chains, processing suspicious third-party payments, or failing to retain customer and supplier due-diligence records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious breaches may result in substantial administrative fines, public or private reprimands, temporary management bans, and restrictions or suspension of activities. Exact sanctions depend on breach classification, turnover, benefit obtained, recurrence, and culpability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may face personal administrative sanctions and, where the conduct facilitates money laundering or another offense, criminal liability, asset confiscation, civil restitution, and judicial precautionary measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal profit distribution or director asset diversion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable profits, disregarding statutory reserves, extracting company assets at undervalue, or paying related parties without corporate benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Invalid or recoverable distributions, repayment obligations, creditor claims, director liability, insolvency consequences, and potential criminal exposure for misappropriation, fraudulent administration, or insolvency offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be required to restore company assets, compensate creditors, repay unlawful distributions, bear insolvency liability, and face civil or criminal sanctions. Limited liability does not shield directors from breach-of-duty claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Modelo 200, Modelo 202, withholding returns, or VAT returns on time, or failure to pay assessed liabilities after the statutory deadline.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing surcharges, late-payment interest, collection surcharges, administrative penalties, enforced collection, bank-account or asset attachment, and potential restriction of tax certificates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur subsidiary liability where they caused or failed to prevent non-payment under the Spanish General Tax Law, particularly during dissolution, cessation, or enforcement scenarios. Imprisonment is not a consequence of ordinary lateness unless the conduct separately constitutes a criminal offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Labor, payroll, or social-security withholding fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying warehouse workers, concealing employment, underreporting payroll, failing to remit employee withholdings, or using sham contractors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Labor and Social Security assessments, surcharges, administrative fines, loss of incentives, joint-liability findings, and potential criminal prosecution for significant fraud or withholding offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may face personal liability, civil restitution, disqualification, and criminal sanctions where intentional concealment or substantial fraud is established.
